blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Manufacturing & Industrial, blockchain & digital trust delivers distributed-ledger programs where a shared, verifiable record has economic value: enterprise dlt networks for multi-party workflows, asset tokenization, smart contract engineering and audit, provenance and traceability, decentralized identity with verifiable credentials, and on-chain analytics for compliance. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise dlt network engineering, asset tokenization & digital assets, smart contract engineering & audit — delivered on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Brownfield instrumentation gap
Critical assets run uninstrumented because gut-and-replace is unthinkable; the data that twins and models need does not exist, and downtime for retrofit is unaffordable.
Quality escapes and manual inspection

Defect detection depends on sampling and eyes; escapes reach customers, and scrap/rework costs hide in the P&L. Vision systems stall in pilot because lighting, thresholds and line integration were never engineered.
Planning by spreadsheet under volatility

Planners fight demand volatility, material shortages and changeovers in spreadsheets; scheduling knowledge lives in two veterans' heads. OEE losses from changeover and waiting are structurally accepted.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 6 services from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower — Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Asset Tokenization & Digital Assets, Smart Contract Engineering & Audit, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: ISO 9001/IATF 16949 quality systems obligations shape the design from the first sprint.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: ISO 9001/IATF 16949 quality systems and ESG reporting (CSRD/ISSB). Plant-level energy and emissions data with auditability. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
